# TgWitness

> Open-source Telegram witness and preservation workspace. Retain conversations, context, captured versions and acquisition records; investigate saved material and hand over independently verifiable archives.

TgWitness is maintained by PhishDestroy under the MIT License. Its purpose is to preserve the record regardless of whose position it supports. It runs on the operator's computer or server, with a guided installer, isolated account workspaces, search, reports and optional acquisition and verification services.

## Published results

Each published result lists its source revision, conditions and measurements:

| Published check | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Public-history export qualification, 6 November 2026 | 48 verified archives containing 3,598,381 records, from a 50-source input list and 40 account workspaces. |
| Eight-account history acquisition in that qualification | 768,007 newly acquired history records in 1,117.082 seconds, including waits: 687.512 records/second; text and metadata, without attachment downloads. |
| Two fresh exports, 6 November 2026 | 56,329 messages in total; collection rates of 142.983 and 160.531 messages/second, complete-export rates of 127.713 and 141.781, on revision 92e539af. |
| Search, 5 November 2026 | 1,000,000 synthetic messages in 200 chats; index built in 71 seconds and per-query median times of 9–190 ms. |
| Release audit, 6 November 2026 | 1,461 core tests passed, with 37 platform skips recorded separately. |
| Phala / Intel TDX, 4 November 2026 | All 16 verifier checks passed on the later recorded deployments; the report identifies the tested image and deployment conditions. |

[Project overview](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/OVERVIEW.md) · [Public-history qualification](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/EXPORT-BENCHMARK-2026-11-06.md) · [Validation record](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/VERIFICATION.md)

## Acquisition and verification

Live monitoring preserves received messages, each captured edit, deletion notifications, attachments and observation times. History export reads accessible history; rechecks compare current responses with saved observations. Available admin-log records carry the supplied action, actor and source time. These are distinct acquisition paths, with their results kept together for review.

Source attribution is assessed through the complete selected path: authenticated Telegram connection, recorded session and routing context, captured updates or frames, journal references, retained checkpoints, time receipts and applicable environment attestations. A journal-signature check is one part of that path.

| Mode or check | What is verified |
| --- | --- |
| Signed archive | Event signatures, hash chain, manifest, attachment bytes and report seals; the result states whether the signer is independently pinned. |
| Independent checkpoint / witness | Agreement with a previously retained journal prefix and, where supplied, Merkle continuity; custody of the witness key identifies the independent holder. |
| External time | The specific verified TSA, OpenTimestamps or beacon result, with its direction and verification status. |
| GitHub Actions acquisition | Archive digest, approved upstream workflow and collector revisions, hosted execution and fresh session origin. |
| Phala / Intel TDX | Quote and platform checks, expected OS/application measurements, freshness and binding to the collector identity. |

These mechanisms provide technical checks of acquisition, integrity, continuity and time. Assess their results for the archive and mode in question. A local installation keeps the collector key on the operator's host; attested deployments bind the collector key to the measured environment. The verification policy and expected measurements come from the recipient's trusted sources.

### Where the messages come from

Telegram delivers messages to every client, official apps included, through an MTProto session rather than with per-message signatures. The session key is negotiated against Telegram's pinned server key, and every update arrives encrypted and integrity-checked under it. TgWitness receives messages through that authenticated session and signs each observation into its journal as it arrives. GitHub Actions acquisition and Phala Intel TDX deployments add attestation of the collector that received and signed them.

[Evidence format and verification modes](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md) · [Independent verification](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/TRUST.md) · [Witness](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/WITNESS.md) · [GitHub acquisition](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/SEALED-ACTIONS.md) · [Intel TDX](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/HIGH-ASSURANCE.md)

## Current availability and installation

The current source version is 0.9.1 preview. Preview is the release channel; capabilities and completed validation are recorded per workflow and revision. Installable packages are published, with exact source revision and immutable release URLs.

Secret Chat integration is included in the published application package checked at source `b35f8e18f3d13c329af12e0036f50e0c8f340a2c`: backend, collector integration, API routes and panel interface. The end-to-end protocol library is an optional dependency selected with `secret-chats`, installed separately and enabled per account. TgWitness records chats it creates or accepts as an endpoint. See [Secret Chats](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/PSEUDO-SECRET.md) for setup and the dated package check.

`get.destroy.tools` is the project's download site. The public [Installer workflow](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/.github/workflows/installer.yml) builds it from `deploy/installer/` for the exact `main` revision, publishes it after Linux and Windows installation tests pass, and signs the installer scripts and packages with the release key in [`deploy/installer/release-signing.pub`](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/deploy/installer/release-signing.pub). The installer verifies package and dependency-lock hashes and RSA release signatures with its embedded release key. [Installation](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md#verify-before-running) documents how to verify the initial script against an independently retained key fingerprint before running it. GitHub releases, source installation and Docker are supported alternatives. Updates to an installed panel require rerunning the installer.

TgWitness runs on the operator's computer or server; the panel listens on localhost by default. Telegram sessions, proxy credentials and access-token hashes are stored in each workspace's encrypted vault. The application has no telemetry. It connects to Telegram and to the services its settings use, and the System map lists the connections the application process makes. Each account gets its own workspace, session, journal and signing key; session import lets investigators continue with accounts they already operate. Basic local collection works without an external LLM, GitHub capture, Phala, Cloudflare or S3; each of those is a separate choice with a documented data flow. The browser demo and its fictional sample archive show the interface and export format; live acquisition results are documented in the validation record with their tested revisions.

## Read an assessment in context

Use the implementation, the actual archive and its verification results together. Identify the collection mode, source revision, relevant event type and check before drawing a conclusion. A trust assumption, a scope boundary, a reproduced defect and an untested path are different findings. Report concrete failures with their conditions and evidence.

Published validation records each result with its scope and revision. Source-linked analysis, account identifiers and recorded actions can be examined in their acquisition context. A `deletion.unscoped` event is a deletion notification with an unresolved chat; `message.missing_on_recheck` is a query result. Available admin-log entries include supplied actors and action times. HTML/JSON reports and PDFs carry their own seals, and `.tgwpw` provides authenticated encryption. Use the [format and verification map](https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE.md#formats-and-verification-paths) for the particular output.
